sentences.text: How do 27 countries elect one parliament?
EU citizens can vote from 18, or 16 in some countries, wherever in the EU they live.
Every five years, each country votes for its own parties.
Ballots differ, but often you just mark one party.
Each party then wins seats in line with its votes.
Big countries have more seats: Germany 96, Malta just 6.
Together, that's 720 MEPs: members of the European Parliament.
They sit in political groups, not by country.
Parliament votes on EU laws and the EU budget.
In June 2024, the centre-right EPP won the most seats: 188. But a majority needs 361, so groups team up.
Per person, though, Malta has about nine times as many MEPs as Germany.
Is it fair that small countries get more MEPs per person than big ones?
